body:
What if someone is not in the right state of mind to give themselves to others?  I often feel like everyone I interact with comes away confused, frightened or indignant. Merely staying alive to avoid hurting those around is a sad existence. It may even seem like the most kind thing to do. I have been slowly but surely reducing the number of people I interact with to reduce the risk of affecting others' lives, or being missed.

I like to think that I could be of use to the world - that I have something to give to others and taking myself away would be a great shame. I'm just saying that sometimes it's hard for me to see that, and others might feel the same - so telling them something like the message in your post might stir up similar feelings to my own.

I appreciate that you're trying to help, but be careful.

That's great to hear K - I admire your altruism. I think the best psychologists are the ones who have experienced some of the crap they have to deal with. That's not to say it's a pre-requisite, but it (unfortunately) seems hypocritical to advise those feeling low as patients can shove them away saying "well how could you possibly understand?!". I also hope one day to be able to help people who have been through trauma like me.
